skills.trigger: When identifying the anatomical position of a radiopaque foreign body on a chest X-ray.
steps: Identify high-density opacities within the thoracic cavity, specifically focusing on the hilar regions where airways branch.
Determine laterality (left vs. right) by referencing the patient's orientation (image left is patient right) and vertebral alignment.
Distinguish the specific location (e.g., right hilum vs. left hilum vs. lung parenchyma) to rule out incorrect lateralization or lobar assignments.

skills.trigger: When explaining why an aspirated foreign body remained asymptomatic or undetected for a prolonged period.
steps: Correlate the shape and orientation of the object seen on endoscopy or X-ray with the axis of the bronchial lumen.
Assess whether the object is aligned longitudinally (parallel to airflow) versus transversely (perpendicular to airflow).

Conclude that longitudinal alignment allows air to pass around or through the object, preventing total obstruction and subsequent symptoms like atelectasis or pneumonia, whereas transverse alignment typically causes immediate blockage.
